{
  "ready_for_offline_gate": false,
  "summary": "Not safe to freeze. The selftests pass, but the checker reports false failures on every CPOL=1 trace, and it misses the TX starvation event that the calibration trace was built to produce. The control harness does not catch the missing event, and the evaluation says there were no event integrity errors. The LSB byte-order logic itself matches the registered amendment. This is a read-only offline audit, not a formal proof.",
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": "F1",
      "severity": "blocking",
      "area": "CPOL idle-level change versus a real serial edge",
      "observation": "All six CPOL=1 probes (write_speed{0,1,2}_mode{2,3}) fail first with cs_framing at cycle 10, with 24 to 73 failures each. In the probe/write_speed0_mode2 trace, command acceptance (dict 127, cpol=1) moves post.sck from 0 to 1 while both CSB lines are still high (csb=3). That is the clock moving to its new idle level. It is not a serial clock edge.",
      "cause": "trans() sends every SCK change to edge(), even when no CSB line is asserted. edge() then pops the queued segment, sees no CSB fall, and reports cs_framing. Every later edge after that is counted with the wrong lead/trail parity.",
      "spec_basis": "Theory lines 35-37 and 241 say CPOL sets the idle level and that configuration takes effect while all CSB lines are deasserted. The spec never calls an idle-level change a leading or trailing edge. Theory line 256 says T_LEAD runs from the CSB fall to the first leading SCK edge, so only edges inside the CSB-asserted window count.",
      "impact": "These are false positives, so the probe results are not evidence of DUT defects. CPHA=1 and CPOL=1 payload, phase and timing checking is effectively unvalidated. The evaluation also lists these as observational failures without raising any concern.",
      "required_fix_scope": "The checker author, not this reviewer, should handle SCK changes while all CSB lines are idle as idle-level moves. Those moves should be checked only against the pending command's CPOL at the next CSB fall. A spurious-SCK rule should still apply when there is no pending segment. Then a clean CPOL=1 control and a CPOL=1 fault control should both be re-run."
    },
    {
      "id": "F2",
      "severity": "blocking",
      "area": "TX starvation event omission",
      "observation": "calibration/tx_starvation_resume returns verdict pass with no events. truncated/tx_starvation_resume returns inconclusive with no events. The control definition for the truncated case requires required_event_family tx_starvation_resume and expects an explicit pending or failed event.",
      "cause_truncated": "The end-of-trace starvation check requires st['wi'] >= len(st['words']). After the last enabled byte of a word is fetched, fetch() leaves bp=4 and does not advance wi until the next fetch. So wi stays below len(words) while the segment is stalled at the boundary, and the condition never holds.",
      "cause_full": "In the complete trace, the detection path inside edge() depends on cur['bnd'], which is set after every 16//w edges, and on the comparison wc >= bnd. This path also produced no event even though a later word resumed the segment. The exact cause was not determined from the packet; a boundary or word-index interaction similar to the truncated case is suspected.",
      "impact": "The requested event tx_starvation_resume is never credited, even on the trace designed to exercise it. A real starvation fault would only be caught through other categories such as tx_underflow, and recovery is never demonstrated.",
      "history_note": "This finding is independent of the earlier, withdrawn underflow claim. This review found no evidence of SCK changes while pre-stalled in the clean calibration."
    },
    {
      "id": "F3",
      "severity": "blocking",
      "area": "Control harness integrity",
      "observation": "event_integrity_errors is empty even though a control's required_event_family is missing. control_counts credits 9 of 10 negatives and says nothing about the missing event.",
      "impact": "The evaluation's apparent completeness is overstated. The harness accepted the event omission described in F2 without flagging it."
    },
    {
      "id": "F4",
      "severity": "major",
      "area": "Independent positive coverage",
      "observation": "All nine independent references, including write_sparse, are Standard-mode, CPOL=0, CPHA=0, FULLCYC=0, CSID 0. There is no independent clean control for CPOL=1, CPHA=1, Dual or Quad, FULLCYC, a held-CS continuation, or a pending CSID change exercised against a real DUT trace.",
      "impact": "False-positive resistance is shown only for the simplest mode, and F1 shows that other modes do produce false positives."
    },
    {
      "id": "F5",
      "severity": "minor",
      "area": "Fault control quality",
      "observation": "negative/clock_during_tx_stall changes only post.sck at one cycle. It is detected through sck_halfperiod (0.5) as an artefact of a two-transition glitch, not through tx_underflow or stall semantics.",
      "impact": "The detection credit is real, but it does not show that the checker detects an SCK pulse during a stall that respects the half-period. That case is uncontrolled."
    },
    {
      "id": "F6",
      "severity": "minor",
      "area": "Full-cycle RX sampling",
      "observation": "With FULLCYC=1 the checker samples action.sd at row+(CLKDIV+1) and requires a stable value across the whole window, otherwise it reports unresolved. This is consistent with the theory diagram (one half SCK later). The contract does not document the assumption that sd_i is captured at that row's rising edge. probe/read_asymmetric_full0 being inconclusive rather than failing is the conservative outcome.",
      "impact": "This is acceptable, but the assumption should be documented. There is no fault control for a word delivered early under FULLCYC, i.e. on the ready boundary."
    },
    {
      "id": "F7",
      "severity": "info",
      "area": "Pending CSID, unsupported modes and resets",
      "observation": [
        "The CSAAT release path accepts either a queued command or a stably offered command (cmd_off) whose CSID or configuration differs. The cmd_off[6:] slice maps correctly to CFG_F, and offers with valid=0 are excluded, which matches the contract.",
        "Speed 3 and Dual/Quad bidirectional segments raise an assumption violation and block checking. Dummy segments are recorded as unresolved and suspend checking.",
        "A software-reset event is capped at pass_unresolved."
      ],
      "impact": "These areas appear correct by inspection, but there is no control for a CSID change offered while ready=0 against real DUT data beyond the selftest."
    },
    {
      "id": "F8",
      "severity": "info",
      "area": "Byte-order authority and isolation",
      "observation": [
        "fetch() visits lanes in increasing index 0 to 3. RX packs byte k at bits 8k and checks high-lane zero padding.",
        "The examples in the amendment are consistent with this.",
        "The superseded lines 698-702 and 735-740 are retained as history.",
        "No DUT source or upstream scoreboard is used.",
        "The amendment is correctly labelled a project interpretation rather than an erratum.",
        "negative/reversed_rx_lanes rejects the old ordering."
      ],
      "impact": "No issue with the amended byte-order logic. The driver contains no expected values and holds inputs per row as specified."
    }
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Static read-only reasoning over the supplied source and traces. No execution, simulation or formal proof was performed.",
    "Six CPOL=0 probe traces were omitted from the packet and were not reviewed.",
    "Trace corruptions are single-fault output edits, not RTL mutants. They give no evidence about B or C effectiveness.",
    "The exact root cause of the full-trace starvation omission (F2) is inferred, not confirmed.",
    "No DUT trace is presumed correct, and the CPOL=1 probe failures are attributed to the checker, not to the DUT.",
    "This review does not authorize B, select targets, or modify any artifact."
  ]
}
```
